hero.title: Find the smallest ST-based reference architecture for retrofit intelligence.
hero.summary: A bounded technical path from local inference, secure identity and physical interfaces to governed real-world action — without tying the architecture to one silicon generation.

situation.title: The engineering question
body: The installed world is the target: sensors, cameras, switches, cabinets, machines and actuators that should gain local intelligence without requiring full replacement.

The immediate question is deliberately narrow: what is the smallest practical ST-based reference architecture that can support local inference, secure identity, physical interfaces and enough headroom for different model classes — and where is the practical boundary between STM32-class devices and more capable ST edge AI options?

theses.title: Carrier-neutral by design
theses.body: The durable object, identity and authority contract should survive replacement of the compute or model carrier. Silicon should implement the architecture, not define it.

theses.title: Local first
theses.body: Sensing and inference should stay local where that reduces latency, bandwidth, cloud dependence and unnecessary data movement.

theses.title: Govern only consequence
theses.body: Not every inference needs heavyweight control. The authority check becomes mandatory when a node can create a real-world effect.

demos.title: Universal Retrofit Intelligence
demos.body: Public architecture for Sense, Perception and Action nodes across existing physical infrastructure. It separates local interpretation from governed consequence.

demos.title: HEIMEL consequence-time authority
demos.body: The control boundary for consequential action: determine whether the exact effect is authorized at the moment it would occur and retain evidence of the decision.

evidence.title: Public edge architecture exists
evidence.body: The Sense → Understand → Govern → Act → Prove flow and the three-node family are already published as the public-safe baseline.

evidence.title: Governance boundary exists
evidence.body: HEIMEL provides the consequence-time authority layer so the hardware exploration can stay focused on local compute, interfaces and execution rather than inventing a second control plane.

evidence.title: Hardware claims remain open
evidence.body: Device choice, power, memory, latency, model fit, cost and interoperability are intentionally not asserted yet. They are the subject of the ST reference-architecture test.

proposal.title: Proposed next step: one bounded ST reference matrix
body: Define three target nodes — Sense, Perception and Action — and map the smallest suitable ST class for each against memory, compute, power, interfaces, security primitives and deployment tooling.

Choose one minimal prototype path, deploy a representative local model, bind identity and the physical effect boundary, and test whether the same higher-level object and authority contract survives a change of compute or model carrier.

The output is not a broad product programme. It is a reference architecture, measured constraints, a working demonstrator and a clear decision on where STM32-class hardware is sufficient and where a more capable ST option becomes necessary.

questions: What is the smallest STM32-class configuration that can support the Sense and basic Perception roles without compromising the architecture?
Where does ST see the practical boundary between STM32-class devices and more capable edge AI hardware for local vision, audio or richer models?
Which secure identity and device-root primitives should be part of the reference design from the start?
Which physical interfaces and development boards give the fastest path to a real sensor-to-action demonstrator?
Which model classes should be used to make the carrier-substitution test technically meaningful rather than synthetic?

cta.title: Define the reference architecture
cta.body: Lock the three node envelopes, candidate ST classes, one prototype workload and the pass/fail criteria for carrier substitution.
